copy.headline: Fort Worth country singer found not guilty after murder trial
copy.caption:
Tarrant County jurors found a local country music artist not guilty following a week-long murder trial. Christopher Blanton Jr., who also goes by the name C’ing Jerome, was acquitted on Friday on charges of murder and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.

During the trial, Blanton’s defense attorneys successfully argued that the 2025 shooting death of 32-year-old Cody Davontae Scott was in self-defense. They told jurors Blanton believed Scott had pointed a gun at him.

story.title: Fort Worth country singer found not guilty after murder trial
story.summary: Tarrant County jurors found a local country music artist not guilty following a week-long murder trial. FORT WORTH, Texas - Tarrant County jurors found a local country music artist not guilty following a week-long murder trial. Christopher Blanton Jr., who also goes by the name C’ing Jerome, was acquitted on Friday on charges of murder and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. During the trial, Blanton’s defense attorneys successfully argued that the 2025 shooting death of 32-year-old Cody Davontae Scott was in self-defense. They told jurors Blanton believed Scott had pointed a gun at him. Prosecutors contended that Scott was unarmed, that it would have been difficult for Blanton to see a weapon if Scott had one, and that the two men had a history of past violent interactions. In a statement provided to FOX 4, Blanton said he has always maintained that he acted in self-defense.…
